standard_prerequisites.use: RGamma(C_total, K) is represented by the totalization Tot_pi of the double complex A^{p,q}.

standard_prerequisites.name: Totalization vanishing
standard_prerequisites.use: If H^{-p}(A^{p, bullet}) = 0 for all p then the cohomology of the product totalization vanishes in degree 0.

core_obligations: Statement (lines 1860-1870): for K in D(C_total): (1) if H^{-p}(C_p, K_p) = 0 for all p >= 0 then H^0(C_total, K) = 0; (2) if RGamma(C_p, K_p) = 0 for all p >= 0 then RGamma(C_total, K) = 0.

Reduction to totalization (proof lines 1872-1878): with the notation of the simplicial cohomology remark, RGamma(C_total, K) is represented by the product totalization Tot_pi of the double complex A^{p,q}; the hypothesis of (1) says H^{-p}(A^{p, bullet}) = 0 for each p.
Vanishing and part (2) (lines 1878-1880): the vanishing in (1) follows from the More on Algebra totalization lemma; part (2) follows from part (1) applied after suitable shifts.
proof_roadmap: Represent RGamma by the product totalization of the componentwise double complex.
Apply the totalization vanishing lemma to the rowwise vanishing hypotheses.
Deduce the derived-level vanishing (2) by shifting.
difficulty_reason: Vanishing lemma (statement 1860-1870, proof 1872-1880): componentwise cohomological vanishing forces global vanishing - the proof represents RGamma by the product totalization (in-source remark), reads the hypothesis as rowwise acyclicity, and applies the More on Algebra totalization vanishing lemma; part (2) follows by shifts; complete short argument. H3.
